{{Short description|Romanian physicist (born 1978)}}
'''Bogdan Andrei Bernevig''' (born 1978 in [[Bucharest]]) is a Romanian professor of [[condensed matter physics]] at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Humboldt-Professur für B. Andrei Bernevig|url=https://www.mpi-halle.mpg.de/bernevig|access-date=2021-04-12|website=www.mpi-halle.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref> His research focuses on [[Topological insulator|topological insulators]] and other topological quantum materials. His work has been awarded numerous prizes, including the 2019 [[James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials|James C. McGroddy Prize]] of the American Physical Society and the 2023 [[EPS Europhysics Prize]].

== Biography ==
Andrei Bernevig took part in the Physics Olympiad in Bucharest from 1994 to 1997 as a teenager (and won international gold and silver medals).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gorzkowski|first=Waldemar|date=2010|title=LIST OF WINNERS IN 1ST – 41ST INTERNATIONAL PHYSICS OLYMPIADS|url=https://www.jyu.fi/tdk/kastdk/olympiads/ipho_winners|url-status=live|access-date=April 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150812140352/http://www.jyu.fi/tdk/kastdk/olympiads/ipho_winners |archive-date=2015-08-12 }}</ref> He graduated from Stanford University (bachelor's degree in physics and master's degree in mathematics in 2001) and received his PhD from Stanford University under [[Shoucheng Zhang]]. As a postdoctoral fellow he went to the Center for Theoretical Physics at Princeton University, where he was appointed Assistant Professor in 2009 and Associate Professor in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Physics - B. Andrei Bernevig|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/b_andrei_bernevig|access-date=2021-04-12|website=physics.aps.org}}</ref>

He deals with the application of topology in solid state physics, for example in the [[fractional quantum hall effect]], and novel topological materials ([[topological insulator]]s, [[topological superconductor]]s) and spin transport or [[spintronics]]. He also deals with ferrous high-temperature superconductors and predicted s-wave pairing there.

== Awards ==
In 2016 he received the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics|New Horizons in Physics Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – B. Andrei Bernevig|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/L156|access-date=2021-04-12|website=breakthroughprize.org|language=en}}</ref> In 2014 he received the [[Sackler Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-09-05|title=Past Laureates of the Raymond and Beverly Sackler International Prize in Physics|url=https://english.tau.ac.il/sackler_prize_in_physics_past_laureates|access-date=2021-04-12|website=Tel Aviv University|language=en-US|archive-date=2017-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016014757/https://english.tau.ac.il/sackler_prize_in_physics_past_laureates}}</ref> In 2017 he was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} B. Andrei Bernevig|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/b-andrei-bernevig/|access-date=2021-04-12|language=en-US}}</ref> and, in 2018, an [[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-10-26|title=Freie Universität Berlin and Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics in Halle Successfully Nominate Scientist for Alexander von Humboldt Professorship|url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/en/presse/informationen/fup/2017/fup_17_296-avh-professur-bernevig/index.html|access-date=2021-04-12|website=www.fu-berlin.de|language=en}}</ref> In 2019 he was awarded the [[James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials]] from the American Physical Society.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prize Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|access-date=2021-04-12|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> He was named a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2022 "for broad and significant contributions to the discovery and understanding of new topological quantum phases".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2022|title=Fellows nominated in 2022|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2022-10-19}}</ref> He was awarded the 2023 [[EPS Europhysics Prize]] jointly with [[Claudia Felser]] for their contributions "in the classification, prediction, and discovery of novel topological quantum materials".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Press release: 2023 EPS Europhysics Prize |url=https://www.cpfs.mpg.de/3639344/20230623b |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids |language=en}}</ref>
